easy.def: Something made by mixing two different kinds.
examples: A mule is a hybrid.
The flower is a hybrid.
A hybrid car uses gas and power.

more.def: A plant or animal that comes from two different kinds, or anything made by mixing two different things.
examples: A mule is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey.
The gardener grew a new hybrid of two rose plants.
A hybrid car runs on both gas and electricity.

easy.def: A street pipe where firefighters get water.
examples: The firefighters used a hydrant.
The hydrant is red.
A hydrant is on the corner.

more.def: A pipe on the street with a valve, where firefighters can get water for their hoses.
examples: The firefighters hooked their hose to the hydrant.
A red hydrant stood on the corner.
Do not park in front of a hydrant.

easy.def: To give your body enough water.
examples: Drink to hydrate.
She hydrated after the run.
Hydrate in the heat.

more.def: To give the body or a plant enough water.
examples: Drink water to hydrate after you play.
The runners hydrated at each stop.
Plants hydrate through their roots.

easy.def: The lightest gas in the world.
examples: Hydrogen is a gas.
Water has hydrogen.
A balloon of hydrogen floats.

more.def: A very light gas that has no color or smell; two parts of it join with oxygen to make water.
examples: Hydrogen is the lightest gas, so a balloon filled with it floats high.
Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
The sun is made mostly of hydrogen.

easy.def: A wild animal like a dog that makes a laughing sound.
examples: A hyena laughed.
The hyena lives in Africa.
We saw a hyena.

more.def: A wild African animal that looks like a dog, has strong jaws and makes a loud, laughing sound.
examples: The hyena let out a laughing call in the dark.
A hyena has powerful jaws that can crush bones.
Hyenas live in groups called clans on the African plains.
We learn about hygiene.
Washing hands is good hygiene.
Hygiene keeps us healthy.

more.def: The habits of keeping yourself and your surroundings clean so that you stay healthy.
examples: Washing your hands with soap is part of good hygiene.
The nurse taught us about hygiene, such as brushing our teeth.
Good hygiene helps stop germs from spreading.

easy.def: A person who cleans teeth at the dentist.
examples: The hygienist cleaned my teeth.
A hygienist works at the dentist.
The hygienist was kind.

more.def: A dental worker who cleans teeth and teaches people how to care for them.
examples: The hygienist cleaned my teeth and showed me how to floss.
A dental hygienist works with the dentist.
The hygienist polished each tooth.

easy.def: A slow, holy song sung in church.
examples: We sang a hymn.
The choir sang a hymn.
I know that hymn.

more.def: A song of praise, usually sung in a church or at a religious service.
examples: The choir sang a hymn in the church on Sunday morning.
Everyone stood up to sing the hymn together.
She learned the words to an old hymn from her grandmother.

easy.def: A lot of loud talk to get people excited about something.
examples: The movie had lots of hype.
Don't believe the hype.
The hype was big.

more.def: A lot of attention or loud advertising that is meant to make people excited about something.
examples: The new game had a lot of hype, but it was only okay.
There was so much hype about the movie that the theater was full.
Do not believe all the hype in the ads.

easy.def: Very excited and full of energy.
examples: The puppy is hyper.
He gets hyper after cake.
She felt hyper.

more.def: Very excited and full of energy, so that it is hard to sit still.
examples: The puppy was hyper and ran in circles.
He gets hyper after eating cake.
The hyper kids could not sit still.

easy.def: A sleepy, dream-like state in which you follow suggestions.
examples: The magician used hypnosis.
Hypnosis is like a dream.
She tried hypnosis.

more.def: A sleepy, dream-like state in which a person is relaxed and follows suggestions, sometimes used to help people feel calm.
examples: The magician pretended to use hypnosis on a volunteer.
Some people try hypnosis to help them relax.
In the cartoon, the swirling wheel put the character under hypnosis.

easy.def: A person who puts people into a sleepy, dreamy state.
examples: The hypnotist did a show.
A hypnotist talks softly.
The hypnotist swung a watch.

more.def: A person who puts others into a deep, dreamy state in which they are very relaxed.
examples: The hypnotist swung a watch in front of the volunteer.
A hypnotist made the audience laugh.
The hypnotist spoke in a soft voice.

easy.def: To put someone in a sleepy, dream-like state.
examples: The swirl hypnotized me.
The magician hypnotized him.
The fire hypnotized us.

more.def: To put a person into a sleepy, dream-like state in which they follow suggestions, or to hold someone's attention completely.
examples: In the cartoon, the swirling wheel hypnotized the cat.
The magician pretended to hypnotize a volunteer on stage.
The glowing fire hypnotized us as we watched the flames.

easy.def: Saying one thing but doing another.
examples: It is hypocritical to say it and not do it.
His hypocritical words did not match.
The hypocritical rule was unfair.

more.def: Telling others to do something that you do not do yourself.
examples: It is hypocritical to tell others to be neat when your own room is messy.
She felt hypocritical for scolding him when she did the same thing.
The hypocritical player told others to follow the rules but broke them.
The joke was hysterical.
We laughed hysterically.
The movie was hysterical.

more.def: So funny that you cannot stop laughing, or wildly upset and out of control.
examples: The clown was hysterical, and we laughed until we cried.
Her costume was hysterical, and the whole class laughed.
The hysterical crowd cheered.
